written:
## 1. The numbers
Risk-on. Tech staged a comeback just days after a selloff that shook Wall Street. The VIX fell sharply, though the Dow was roughly flat.

## 2. What moved and why
**AI trade bounces back and lifts the Nasdaq**
Why it happened: Nvidia jumped 4% and CoreWeave soared 24% after an upbeat outlook. OpenAI's quarterly revenue reached $10 billion, and Anthropic's IPO was reportedly multiple times oversubscribed.
Why it matters: The selloff had raised doubts about AI spending, and these results suggest demand is still there. Gains were concentrated in tech, so breadth is a question.

**Fed hike bets build after hot data**
Why it happened: Investors shifted their bets toward a Fed rate hike next month. The October jobs report was red hot and beat all Wall Street estimates.
Why it matters: A Fed that is raising rates, not cutting them, keeps pressure on bond prices and on equity valuations.

**Dollar firms, loonie slips**
Why it happened: The dollar index rose 0.31% and USD/CAD rose 0.38% to 1.4242. The likely driver is the repricing toward a Fed hike, though no source ties the two directly.
Why it matters: A weaker loonie raises import costs for Canadian firms. It helps exporters who earn US dollars.

## Deals
- **Acquisition: Marvell → Lumentum** (about $115B). The logic is to build a leader in AI connectivity.
- **Acquisition: Strathcona Resources → Greenfire Resources** (up to C$2.9B including debt). The deal combines two long-life oilsands and heavy oil companies.
- **Acquisition: National Bank of Canada → Embark Student Corp.** (about C$226M). The bank is buying digital capability and a base of education-savings customers.

## Already out today
- Before the open: CoreWeave Q3 earnings. Revenue beat expectations; 2026 guidance raised. It is a strong read on AI infrastructure demand.
- By 8 AM: easyJet shareholder votes on Apollo takeover. 97.07% backed the court resolution; 96.67% backed the general meeting resolution. No consensus figure was available. The cash offer of 715p per share values the airline at about £5.7 billion.
- : October CPI. 337.51 vs 337.02 expected. A small beat on the headline index level; economists had flagged a core print of 0.3% or higher would strengthen the case for a December hike.

## 3. What's coming today
- Thu: Fed speakers, led by Williams. Hammack, who dissented in October, speaks that morning.
- Fri: Producer prices (PPI). Follows Thursday's Fed speakers.
Nothing major is scheduled for the rest of today. Thu 8:30 AM: (the brief lists this time with no event attached, so it is left unspecified). Upcoming: Fed speakers led by Williams on Thursday, and Producer prices on Friday.

## 4. Canada corner
- USD/CAD rose 0.38% to 1.4242. A weaker loonie raises import costs for Canadian firms and helps exporters who earn US dollars.
- Canadian 10-year yield is 3.63%, well below the US 10-year at 4.88%.

## 5. The takeaway
Tech's rebound shows the AI trade can outweigh rate fears for now, but a Fed hike bet keeps the next move in rates the key risk.

stories.full: Last week's selloff included the Nasdaq's worst session in 18 months. Today's bounce is a partial reversal, with the Nasdaq up 1.90% and the S&P 500 up 1.26%. The catalyst was CoreWeave. The neocloud company beat third-quarter revenue expectations and raised its 2026 operating income and revenue guidance. That helped Nvidia, which was at about $175 and up 4%. The Bloomberg wrap also cited the OpenAI revenue figure and the Anthropic IPO demand as further evidence. Winners are AI infrastructure names. stories.title: Fed hike bets build after hot data
stories.why_happened: Investors shifted their bets toward a Fed rate hike next month. The October jobs report was red hot and beat all Wall Street estimates.
stories.why_matters: A Fed that is raising rates, not cutting them, keeps pressure on bond prices and on equity valuations.
stories.full: The Fed raised rates in September, and two officials voted for another hike in October. Since then the data has not made a pause easy to argue. October CPI was released yesterday. The index came in at 337.51 against a consensus of 337.02. That is a small beat on the headline index level. Economists had flagged that a core print of 0.3% or higher would strengthen the case for a December hike. The US 10-year yield sits at 4.88%. Stocks have so far looked through the hike talk. Hammack, who dissented in October, speaks that morning. Producer prices follow on Friday.

stories.title: Dollar firms, loonie slips
stories.why_happened: The dollar index rose 0.31% and USD/CAD rose 0.38% to 1.4242. The likely driver is the repricing toward a Fed hike, though no source ties the two directly.
stories.why_matters: A weaker loonie raises import costs for Canadian firms. It helps exporters who earn US dollars.
stories.full: Higher expected US rates tend to support the dollar against other currencies. That fits today's pattern, where the US dollar index and USD/CAD both moved up. The Canadian 10-year yield is 3.63%, well below the US 10-year at 4.88%. A wide gap favours the US dollar. Oil is near $100 a barrel (WTI 99.64). Canadian energy exports are priced in US dollars, so a weaker loonie lifts their Canadian-dollar value. Importers, and anyone with US-dollar debt, lose out. Watch Thursday's Fed speakers and Friday's PPI. A hotter read would likely push the dollar higher again.

deals.why: The logic is to build a leader in AI connectivity.
deals.full: Marvell announced an all-stock agreement on November 2 to buy Lumentum, the largest semiconductor acquisition of 2026. Marvell's CEO called the deal a once-in-a-generation move to create a dominant AI connectivity player. Payment is entirely in stock, so Lumentum holders become owners of the combined company. The sources I found do not report a per-share price or premium. The rationale is vertical integration. Data centres need faster links between chips, and Marvell is paying up to own more of that stack. Size matters here. At $115B, this is among the biggest deals in the sector. It signals that AI infrastructure is still pulling in large strategic capital. It also shows boards are willing to use richly valued stock as currency.

deals.why: The deal combines two long-life oilsands and heavy oil companies.
deals.full: The deal values Greenfire at C$2.7 billion to C$2.9 billion, including debt. Greenfire holders can choose 0.25 of a Strathcona share or $11 in cash per share. Greenfire closed at $7.93 on Friday, so the cash option is about a 39% premium (my calculation). The stock option is worth about $9.09 at Strathcona's $36.34 close. Waterous Energy Fund holds 72% of Greenfire and 57% of Strathcona. It backs the deal and plans to take shares. Greenfire's leadership will keep running its assets as a Strathcona business unit. It signals continued consolidation in Canadian oil sands, with a common owner on both sides.

deals.why: The bank is buying digital capability and a base of education-savings customers.
deals.full: The price is estimated at $226 million, subject to working capital adjustments. The bank expects its CET1 ratio to fall by about 10 basis points on closing. The bank will buy the shares from the Foundation. The logic is to add a digital RESP platform. Embark will keep applying for government grants for customers and investing RESP funds. The small capital hit shows Canadian banks can still do bolt-on deals without straining capital.

intern.headline: Tech bounces back as AI demand signals calm markets
intern.mood: Risk-on (investors are willing to take bigger bets). Tech made a comeback just days after a selloff (a sharp drop in prices) that shook Wall Street. The VIX (a gauge of how nervous investors are) fell sharply, but the Dow (an index of 30 large US companies) was roughly flat.

stories.title: AI trade bounces back and lifts the Nasdaq
stories.why_happened: Nvidia (a company that makes chips for AI) jumped 4%. CoreWeave (a company that rents out computing power for AI) soared 24% after an upbeat outlook (a positive forecast for future business). OpenAI's quarterly revenue reached $10 billion. Anthropic's IPO (the first time a company sells its shares to the public) was reportedly multiple times oversubscribed (many more people wanted shares than were available).
stories.why_matters: The selloff had raised doubts about AI spending. These results suggest demand for AI is still strong. But most of the gains came from tech, so it is unclear whether the rally will spread to other areas.
stories.full: Last week's selloff included the Nasdaq's worst session in 18 months. Today's bounce is a partial reversal (only part of the drop was won back), with the Nasdaq up 1.90% and the S&P 500 (an index of 500 large US companies) up 1.26%. The catalyst was CoreWeave. The neocloud company (a newer type of cloud computing firm built for AI) beat third-quarter revenue expectations and raised its 2026 operating income and revenue guidance (its official forecast for the year). That helped Nvidia, which was at about $175 and up 4%. The Bloomberg wrap (a daily market summary) also cited the OpenAI revenue figure and the Anthropic IPO demand as more evidence. Winners are AI infrastructure names (companies that build the basic systems AI runs on). The Dow was down slightly at the open. The Russell 2000 (an index of smaller US companies) stayed under pressure, so the move was not even across the market. The VIX dropped to 17.77. Watch whether the rally spreads beyond the biggest tech companies. Also watch whether rate worries return, since higher yields (the interest rate on bonds) make fast-growing companies look less valuable.

stories.title: Fed hike bets build after hot data
stories.why_happened: Investors shifted their bets toward a Fed (the US central bank) rate hike next month. The October jobs report was red hot (much stronger than expected) and beat all Wall Street estimates.
stories.why_matters: A Fed that is raising rates, instead of cutting them, keeps pressure on bond prices and on stock prices (equity valuations).
stories.full: The Fed raised rates in September. Two officials voted for another hike in October. Since then, the data has not made a pause easy to argue for. October CPI (the main measure of consumer prices) was released yesterday. The index came in at 337.51, against a consensus (the average forecast of economists) of 337.02. That is a small beat on the headline index level. Economists had said a core print (inflation without food and energy) of 0.3% or higher would strengthen the case for a December hike. The US 10-year yield (the interest rate on the US 10-year government bond) sits at 4.88%. Stocks have so far looked past the talk of hikes. The bounce in tech shows investors are weighing AI earnings more heavily than rates today. Next up is a run of Fed speakers on Thursday, led by Williams. Hammack, who voted against the majority in October, speaks that morning. Producer prices (a measure of what companies pay for goods) come out on Friday.

stories.title: Dollar firms, loonie slips
stories.why_happened: The dollar index (a score of the US dollar against a basket of other currencies) rose 0.31%. USD/CAD (how many Canadian dollars one US dollar buys) rose 0.38% to 1.4242. The likely driver is the repricing toward a Fed hike, though no source ties the two directly.
stories.why_matters: A weaker loonie (the nickname for the Canadian dollar) makes imports more expensive for Canadian firms. It helps exporters who earn US dollars.
stories.full: Higher expected US rates tend to support the dollar against other currencies. That fits today's pattern, where the US dollar index and USD/CAD both moved up. The Canadian 10-year yield is 3.63%, well below the US 10-year at 4.88%. A wide gap like this favours the US dollar, because investors can earn more by holding US bonds. Oil is near $100 a barrel (WTI 99.64). WTI is a common type of oil. Canadian energy exports are priced in US dollars, so a weaker loonie lifts their value in Canadian dollars. Importers, and anyone with US-dollar debt (money borrowed in US dollars), lose out. Watch Thursday's Fed speakers and Friday's PPI. A hotter read would likely push the dollar higher again.

deals.why: Marvell announced an all-stock agreement on November 2 to buy Lumentum. It is the largest semiconductor acquisition (a company buying a chip maker) of 2026. The goal is to build a leader in AI connectivity (the links that connect AI computers).
deals.full: Marvell's CEO called the deal a once-in-a-generation move to create a dominant AI connectivity player. Payment is entirely in stock, so Lumentum shareholders become owners of the combined company. The sources I found do not report a per-share price or premium (the extra amount paid above the current share price). The reason is vertical integration (owning more steps of the same supply chain). Data centres (buildings full of computers) need faster links between chips, and Marvell is paying to own more of that setup. Size matters here. At $115B, this is among the biggest deals in the sector. It shows that AI infrastructure is still attracting large investments from companies. It also shows that company bosses are willing to use their highly valued stock to pay for deals.

deals.why: The deal combines two long-life oilsands and heavy oil companies.
deals.full: The deal values Greenfire at C$2.7 billion to C$2.9 billion, including debt (money the company owes). Greenfire shareholders can choose either 0.25 of a Strathcona share or $11 in cash per share. Greenfire closed at $7.93 on Friday, so the cash option is about a 39% premium (the extra amount paid above the current share price, my calculation). The stock option is worth about $9.09 at Strathcona's $36.34 close. Waterous Energy Fund holds 72% of Greenfire and 57% of Strathcona. It backs the deal and plans to take shares. Greenfire's leadership will keep running its assets as a Strathcona business unit (a part of the bigger company). It shows that Canadian oil sands companies (firms that get oil from thick sand deposits) keep joining together, and one owner sits on both sides.

deals.why: Embark manages RESPs (Canadian savings accounts for education) for about 436,000 beneficiaries. The bank is buying digital capability and a base of education-savings customers.
deals.full: The price is estimated at $226 million, subject to working capital adjustments (small changes based on the company's cash and short-term money at closing). The bank expects its CET1 ratio (a key measure of a bank's financial strength) to fall by about 10 basis points (0.10%) at closing. The bank will buy the shares from the Foundation. The reason is to add a digital RESP platform. Embark will keep applying for government grants for customers and investing RESP funds. The small effect on the bank's strength shows Canadian banks can still make smaller deals without putting strain on their finances.

results.why: A strong sign that demand for AI computing infrastructure is still growing.

results.actual: 97.07% backed the court resolution; 96.67% backed the general meeting resolution
results.why: Shareholders strongly support the takeover. The cash offer of 715p per share values the airline at about £5.7 billion. No consensus figure was available.
A small upside surprise on the headline price index, adding to the case for another Fed rate hike.

intern.takeaway: Markets can bounce back fast when big companies show strong demand. But rising interest rates can still pull stock prices down.
intern.takeaway_accounting: Accounting tip: when a company buys another, the numbers on its books change, so check the deal terms and how the price was paid.
intern.takeaway_consulting: Consulting tip: look for the reason behind each deal. Here, companies are buying to own more of the AI supply chain.
